positions.commentary: Google is capable of going after AI opportunities with its existing business structure.
McDonald's is not well equipped to handle salads because their production line and brand perception differ from fresh salad concepts.

IBM had a great business with on-prem servers for a long time, but abandoning it early to focus on the next thing might not have made sense from a profit perspective over the lifetime of the business.
The speaker mentions Tesla as an example of a clean startup doing well in the EV market alongside BYD.
Altria Group generated great cash flow from cigarettes but had poor capital allocation by investing in new technologies like marijuana and alcohol instead of returning cash to shareholders.
Mark Zuckerberg made a big mistake with Facebook by not allowing more control over who users were sharing with early on.

thesis: This episode argues that established companies often fail not because they lack capability, but because they abandon profitable legacy businesses too early or fail to adapt their supply chains and brand perception to new categories like salads. It suggests that clean startups like Tesla succeed due to organizational agility, while legacy firms like Google and Meta face mixed outcomes as they attempt to disrupt themselves with AI or chase new content vectors without fully retaining their core user comforts.
